data.description:
# Investigate why completed plan/intake sessions are not closed on completion

## Problem statement

Pi agent sessions launched in Herdr panes run `pi` in **interactive** mode with
an initial prompt (`packages/herdr/shared/run-pi-agent.sh`). When a skill
completes it emits a `</end_session>` marker, but nothing consumes that marker:
the interactive REPL simply waits for the next input, so the pane and its
~200 MB pi process stay alive forever. Over hours these abandoned sessions
accumulate — the operator observed **50 concurrent pi sessions / ~12.4 GB RSS
with ages up to 18+ hours**, contributing to severe CPU oversubscription
(load ~3× cores). Nothing transitions the session to a closed state on skill
completion, and there is no lifecycle hook that reaps sessions whose agent died
without emitting the marker.

## Users

- **Operator / producer** — wants completed agent panes to disappear on their
  own so the machine is not oversubscribed and panes do not need manual pruning.
- **Downtime dispatcher** — spawns intake/plan/audit/risk-effort panes for every
  dispatched item; if those panes never close, the dispatcher floods the host.
- **Agents** — need their session to end cleanly (lease released, pane torn
  down) once their task and report are complete, without an operator click.

Example user stories:

- As an operator, when a dispatched `/skill:intake` or `/skill:plan` session
  finishes and writes its `</end_session>` report, I want the pane to close
  automatically so idle sessions do not accumulate.
- As a producer, I want an agent that stops to ask me a question (no
  `</end_session>`) to keep its pane open so I can answer it, but an agent whose
  process died silently to be cleaned up.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **AC1 — graceful auto-close on completion.** When a session's final
   assistant message's concatenated text, `.rstrip()`-ed, ends with
   `</end_session>`, the pane is closed programmatically by the shared closure
   script so the process exits, the pane is torn down, and the proxy model
   lease is released — with no operator action. (Mechanism revised in planning:
   an in-process `agent_end`/`agent_settled` hook is NOT used, because the SDK
   exposes no `agent_settled` event and `agent_end` proved unreliable; the
   scheduled closure script owns this — see Appendix Q5.) Metric: a unit test
   with a fixture session whose last assistant text ends with the marker asserts
   a close is requested exactly once; an end-to-end check shows the pane closes
   within one reaper interval.
2. **AC2 — no false positives.** No close is requested when the final
   assistant message does not end with the marker — including a `</end_session>`
   quoted mid-message, a question-ended session, an aborted run, and a run that
   ended in a non-retryable error. Metric: negative-path unit tests for each
   case assert zero close requests, and an item with
   `needsProducerReview=true` is never auto-closed.
3. **AC3 — marker-less sessions are reaped (fail-closed).** Sessions whose agent
   died or was killed without emitting the marker do not linger indefinitely: a
   liveness/idle reaper closes panes whose agent process is gone or idle beyond
   a configurable threshold (default 30 minutes, per producer decision), while **never**
   closing a pane that is actively working, has live child processes, or has
   `needsProducerReview=true`. Metric: table-driven classifier tests plus an
   integration check on a synthetic abandoned pane.
4. **AC4 — `implement` panes remain excluded** from automatic close, preserving
   the AC6 precedent of `WL-0MU308WSF0002JWN` unless the producer explicitly
   changes the policy. Metric: a test asserts an `implement` pane is never
   auto-closed.
5. **AC5 — child processes are not orphaned.** When a session exits or is
   terminated, its spawned children (e.g. audit/plan runners) are terminated
   with it, so none are reparented to PID 1. Metric: an integration test spawns
   a long-running child in a session-scoped process group, terminates the
   session, and asserts the child does not survive.
6. **AC6 — one shared idle/completion classifier.** The automatic hook and the
   `pane-triage` skill (`WL-0MUJMXVPO0016DZM`) consume a single
   marker-detection + liveness helper, so the two mechanisms cannot diverge.
   Metric: both call the shared module; its classifier is covered by
   table-driven tests (marker at end accepted; marker mid-message rejected).
7. **AC7 — tests and documentation.** Unit and integration tests are added for
   every path. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes,
   including code comments, `packages/tui/extensions/README.md`, and any
   relevant `docs/` entries. Full project test suite must pass with the new
   changes.

## Constraints

- Must not close a pane that is actively working **or** awaiting a producer
  answer.
- Mechanism (revised in planning): closure is performed by a scheduled,
  out-of-process closure script that reads session logs — NOT by an in-process
  `agent_end` hook. The script must never race the existing `agent_end`
  recovery/compaction flow: it only closes a pane whose session is demonstrably
  settled (idle beyond the threshold, or its agent process is gone).
- The existing downtime auto-close logic (`pane-lifecycle.ts`,
  `WL-0MU308WSF0002JWN`) must remain intact and must not double-handle or race
  the new closure script; both must be idempotent.
- Auto-close must be configurable/overridable (threshold, on/off) so an operator
  can disable it without editing code.
- Headless modes (JSON/RPC) must be unaffected; gate UI-facing behaviour to TUI
  mode as `herdr-agent-state.ts` already does.
- Never close the invoking/current operator pane.

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/shared/run-pi-agent.sh` runs `pi` (interactive) with an
  initial prompt; on `pi` exit its `EXIT` trap calls
  `release-lease-on-exit.mjs` and Herdr tears the pane down when the primary
  process exits. **The gap is that `pi` never exits.**
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/` is the auto-loaded pi extension
  (`index.ts` wires activity indicator, model display, session health,
  guardrails, skill-path, recovery, lease release). It hooks `agent_end`,
  `session_shutdown`, `agent_start` and `turn_end`. Note: the pi SDK exposes
  **no** `agent_settled` event (verified against
  `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent` `ExtensionAPI` types), so an
  `agent_settled`-based hook is not implementable as originally drafted.
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/register-recovery.ts` inspects
  the last assistant message on `agent_end` — a precedent for reading final
  output, and a coordination point so recovery finishes before shutdown.
- `packages/herdr/src/pane-lifecycle.ts` classifies **dispatched** panes by
  worklog stage and closes everything except `implement`; it only covers panes
  recorded in `.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log`, so manually opened and
  marker-less panes are never reaped.
- `~/.pi/agent/extensions/herdr-agent-state.ts` reports `idle`/`working`/
  `blocked` to Herdr but never closes anything.
- The report helper (`~/.pi/agent/skills/report/scripts/render_report.py`)
  appends the canonical `</end_session>` marker and is emitted by every skill's
  end-of-session report.
- Observed evidence: 44–50 live `pi` processes (~200 MB RSS each), sessions with
  completed work still alive, and orphaned `audit_runner` children reparented to
  PID 1.

## Desired change

Build an out-of-process, script-driven session-closure capability (revised in
planning — see Appendix Q5):

1. A **shared closure classifier** (pure logic, table-driven tests) that
   decides, for one session/pane: idle-with-marker, idle-without-marker
   (agent process gone or idle beyond the 30-minute threshold), active, or
   never-close (`implement`, `needsProducerReview=true`, invoking pane).
2. A **closure script** (CLI) that scans herdr panes, classifies each via the
   shared classifier, and closes eligible panes idempotently, writing a ledger.
   This is the programmatic handler; it does not depend on the unreliable
   in-process `agent_end` event.
3. The script is **scheduled** to run periodically (herdr downtime-worker tick
   or equivalent) with on/off + threshold configuration, and is idempotent
   against the existing `pane-lifecycle.ts` dispatch monitor.
4. Session-scoped child processes are terminated on closure so none are
   orphaned to PID 1.
5. The **`pane-triage` skill** (`WL-0MUJMXVPO0016DZM`) reuses the same
   classifier/script rather than re-deriving idle state from the session log
   (coordination: comment + dependency edge).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/pane-close.ts` — **new**: shared closure classifier (marker detection + liveness + close eligibility). Pure, no I/O.
- `packages/herdr/src/pane-close.test.ts` — **new**: table-driven classifier tests.
- `packages/herdr/src/pane-close-reaper.ts` — **new**: closure script orchestration (scan → classify → close → ledger), injectable I/O.
- `packages/herdr/src/pane-close-reaper.test.ts` — **new**: fixture-based reaper tests (exclusions, idempotence, no-op).
- `packages/herdr/src/process-group.ts` + `.test.ts` — **new**: session-scoped child-process teardown.
- `packages/herdr/src/pane-lifecycle.ts` — existing dispatch-pane classifier; keep intact, de-duplicate against the new closure script.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — periodic wiring/scheduling of the closure script.
- `packages/herdr/shared/run-pi-agent.sh` — reference only (exit/lease-release path).
- `packages/tui/extensions/README.md` — document the closure script and its configuration.
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/report/scripts/render_report.py` — reference only (marker source).

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** `</end_session>` is the single canonical terminal signal and
  is always the final line of a completed skill report.
- **Risk — premature close.** An in-process `agent_end` hook could race
  recovery/compaction. Mitigated by the planning decision to close
  out-of-process from a scheduled script that requires the session to be
  settled (agent process gone, or idle beyond the 30-minute threshold).
- **Risk — false-positive close** of an interactive session mid-conversation;
  mitigated by strict final-message marker matching plus negative-path tests.
- **Risk — scope creep.** Orphaned-child reaping and the marker-less reaper
  overlap existing work; if either grows large it should become a child item
  rather than inflate this fix.
- **Risk — double handling.** The downtime `pane-lifecycle` monitor may race
  the new closure script; both must be idempotent and the winner must be
  deterministic.
- **Risk — marker-less session misclassification.** A genuinely working agent
  that is silent for >30 minutes could be reaped. Mitigated by requiring the
  agent process to be gone OR the idle threshold to be exceeded, plus
  live-child-process and `needsProducerReview` guards.

## Related work

- `WL-0MUJMXVPO0016DZM` — Create pane-triage skill: gated close of idle panes (manual complement; reuses the shared classifier/script — see Appendix Q1/Q5).
- `WL-0MU308WSF0002JWN` — Log all dispatches and auto close all completed dispatch panes, except implement (precedent; `implement` exception).
- `WL-0MU4US5MP001JFEN` — Implement auto-close logic with implement exception.
- `WL-0MSGI7UIH008USVB` — Herdr plugin: release the Local Proxy model lease when a pi session is closed (exit/release path).
- `WL-0MUJLCVRS0093EJJ` — Create a machine-hygiene skill that evaluates performance pressure (orphaned audit_runners, stale servers).
- `WL-0MSB19J56006E87J` — Investigate excessive wl process spawning (206 concurrent, ~17 GB RAM).
- `WL-0MRP1SLZB005ZNYO` — Fix orphaned ContextHub node processes that never exit after worktree cleanup.
- `WL-0MSMGGPWR000MZ0O` — Auto-continue after mid-session compaction (session lifecycle precedent).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — Deferral to the pane-triage skill (`WL-0MUJMXVPO0016DZM`).**
  Should this item defer to pane-triage, or own the automatic lifecycle fix?
  **Answer (producer, 2026-09-27):** Keep both. This item owns the automatic
  fix; pane-triage remains the approval-gated manual complement. Rationale:
  pane-triage's idle test is the same `</end_session>` marker and it never
  closes anything unattended, so it cannot prevent accumulation (50
  sessions/18h accumulated despite the operator being available), and it is
  blind to sessions whose agent died without emitting the marker. **Final:
  no deferral.** The producer further directed that a *script* perform the
  programmatic closure and that pane-triage reuse that script so the two
  cannot diverge (see Q5). This supersedes the earlier OPEN QUESTION.
- **Q2 — Marker-less / crashed sessions.**
  Is a gated manual close sufficient, or is an automatic liveness/idle reaper
  required? **Answer (producer):** automatic, fail-closed reaper is required
  (AC3), because marker-less sessions are invisible to pane-triage and
  dominated the observed backlog. **Final: automatic reaper.**
- **Q3 — Orphaned child-process cleanup (AC5) scope.**
  In scope here or a separate child item? **Answer (producer):** focus here —
  AC5 stays in this item (not split out). **Final: in scope.**
- **Q5 — Closure mechanism (in-process hook vs out-of-process script).**
  `agent_end` was found unreliable and the SDK exposes no `agent_settled`
  event. **Answer (producer):** do not rely on `agent_end`; write a script
  that programmatically handles the closures, and coordinate with
  `WL-0MUJMXVPO0016DZM` so the pane-triage skill uses the script. **Final:
  out-of-process, scheduled closure script + shared classifier.**
- **Q6 — Idle threshold for the marker-less reaper.** **Answer (producer):**
  30 minutes. **Final: default 30 minutes, configurable.**
- **Q7 — Placement of the shared script.** **Open (assumption).**
  Recommended: ContextHub `packages/herdr/` (the pure classifier, CLI and
  scheduler live beside the existing `pane-lifecycle.ts`, and herdr's build
  and tests already cover them); the pane-triage skill (SorraAgents
  `skill/pane-triage/`) invokes the script. Alternative: place the CLI inside
  `SorraAgents/skill/pane-triage/scripts/` (crosses repos). Recorded as an
  assumption to validate at implementation.

## Plan: changelog

- **2026-09-27** — Initial decomposition. Revised AC1/AC2/AC3 and the
  mechanism from an in-process `agent_end` hook to a scheduled, out-of-process
  closure script + shared classifier (producer decision, Appendix Q5/Q6);
  resolved Appendix Q1–Q3; split work into test-first child items. Session:
  see session-logging comment.
- **Q4 — Does `</end_session>` align with the session-close lifecycle?**
  **Answer (agent research):** Partially. It is the correct primary signal for
  graceful completions, but the pane-triage model misses sessions that died
  without emitting it. Evidence: live idle `pi` REPLs with completed work, plus
  `audit_runner` children reparented to PID 1 (parent died, no marker).
  Source: process inspection, `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/*`,
  `~/.pi/agent/skills/report/scripts/render_report.py`.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MSMDYJ3X00895MP** – Show complete, right-aligned model name on footer Line 3 (remove 30-col truncation) (completed)
- **WL-0MSIXMKOX0052514** – Align wl init with SorraAgents install: delegate agent-guidance/workflow setup instead of duplicating (completed)
- **WL-0MUBVKXQJ000L8EO** – In-flight guard: Herdr-head and normal scan paths (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: 0msgi7uih008usvb, abandoned, ac1, ac2, ac3 (+350 more)
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — matched: aborted, ac1, ac2, ac3, ac5 (+293 more)
- `CLI.md` — matched: actively, add, added, agent, agents (+280 more)
